• The implied meaning of the given sentence is: Although he has a very terrible illness, he will recover.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence:** *His disease is no doubt very serious but he will pull through__.*

• An **adverb **is a word or phrase that modifies or qualifies an adjective, verb, or other adverb or a word group, expressing a relation of place, time, circumstance, manner, cause, degree, etc.
 
• **Lovingly **means with love or great care.
 
 
• **Example -** *They smile lovingly at each other.*
 
 
 
• Love is a noun, which means an intense feeling of deep affection.

• Adjectives describe or modify nouns and limit or restrict the meaning of nouns and pronouns.
 
• **The implied meaning of the sentence is:** As the nurse brought the infant in, the mother gave her a kind gaze.
 
• So, an adverb should be used here.

questions.question: In an election that was contested by 2 candidates, one candidate got 20% of the total votes and yet lost by 600 votes. What is the total number of votes cast in the election assuming all votes are valid?

Percentage of votes got by losing candidates = 20%

Number of votes by which losing candidate lost = 600 votes

Concept used:

Total number of votes = Number of votes secured by A + Number of votes secured by B

Calculation:

Let the total number of votes be x.

Number of votes losing candidate got = x × (20/100)

⇒ 0.20x

Number of votes winning candidate got = 0.20x + 600

Then, Total number of votes = 0.20x + 0.20x + 600 = x

⇒ 0.40x + 600 = x

⇒ x – 0.40x = 600

⇒ 0.60x = 600

⇒ x = 1000

∴ The total number of votes is 1000.

questions.question: If (a - 1)² + (b + 2)² + (c - 1)² = 0, the the value of a² + b² + c² is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the sum of squares is exactly zero, each base term must equal zero.

a − 1 = 0 ⇒ a = 1

b + 2 = 0 ⇒ b = −2

c − 1 = 0 ⇒ c = 1

a² + b² + c² = 1² + (−2)² + 1² = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(a − 1)² + (b + 2)² + (c − 1)² = 0

**Concept Used:**

For any real numbers x, y, and z, if x² + y² + z² = 0, then each individual number must be zero because the square of a real number cannot be negative.

x = 0, y = 0, z = 0

**Calculation:**

⇒ (a − 1)² = 0 ⇒ a − 1 = 0 ⇒ a = 1

⇒ (b + 2)² = 0 ⇒ b + 2 = 0 ⇒ b = −2

⇒ (c − 1)² = 0 ⇒ c − 1 = 0 ⇒ c = 1

Now, substitute the values of a, b, and c into the required expression:

⇒ a² + b² + c²

⇒ (1)² + (−2)² + (1)²

⇒ 1 + 4 + 1

⇒ 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Property

Since the square of any real number is always non-negative, the sum of multiple squared terms can only result in zero if every individual term is exactly zero.

Important Algebraic Identity

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). This formula frequently connects the sum of squares with the sum of terms and their cross-products.

Quadratic Minimum

A perfect square expression like (x − k)² achieves its lowest possible real minimum value of 0 exactly when x = k.

questions.question: When the commodity value of money is less than the monetary value of money, it is called _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Credit money**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The commodity value of money is less than the monetary value of money, it is called** Credit money.**
 
• **Credit money** is monetary value created as the result of some future obligation or claim.
 
• As such, credit money emerges from the extension of credit or issuance of debt. In the modern** fractional reserve banking** system, commercial banks are able to create credit money by issuing loans in greater amounts than the reserves they hold in their vaults.
 
• There are many forms of credit money, such as** IOUs, bonds and money markets.** 
 
• Virtually any form of **financial instrument** that cannot or is not meant to be repaid immediately can be construed as a form of credit money.
 
• Credit money is the **creation of monetary value** through the establishment of future claims, obligations, or debts.
 
• These **claims or debts** can be transferred to other parties in exchange for the value embodied in these claims.
 
• **Fractional reserve banking** is a common way that credit money is introduced in modern economies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiat money** is a government-issued currency that is not backed by a physical commodity, such as gold or silver, but rather by the government that issued it.
 
• Any money whose face value (exchange value) is equal to its intrinsic value (the worth of the metallic content of money) is called full-bodied money
 
• Fiduciary money is money that is accepted as a medium of exchange due to the trust that exists between the payer and the payee.

__
 
• Species of moss are used as fuel to **provide peat that has long been used as fuel.**
 
• Mosses are nonvascular plants also known as **Bryophytes**.
 
• **Sphagnum** is commonly known as peat moss.
 
• Peat has multiple uses as it provides **nutrients** to them and also it is used to derive energy which could be used in vehicles.
 
• **Peat** is used for domestic heating purposes as an alternative to** firewood **and forms a fuel suitable for boiler firing in either **briquetted or pulverized** form.
 
• **Peat** is also used for **household cooking** in some places and has been used to produce** small amounts of electricity.**
 
• Some organizations classify peat as** fossil fuel** and not as a renewable fuel.
 
• The development of peat is favoured by **warm moist climatic conditions**; however, peat can develop even in cold regions such as Siberia, Canada, and Scandinavia. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mosses **are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division **Bryophyta**.
 
• **Bryophyta** may also refer to the parent group of bryophytes, which comprise liverworts, mosses, and hornworts.
 
• Mosses typically form dense **green clumps** or **mats**, often in damp or shady locations.
 
• The individual plants are usually composed of **simple leaves** that are generally only one cell thick, attached to a stem that may be branched or unbranched and has only a limited role in conducting water and nutrients.
 
• Although some species have **conducting tissues**, these are generally poorly developed and structurally different from similar tissue found in vascular plants.
 
• **Mosses** do not have seeds and after fertilisation develop sporophytes with unbranched stalks topped with single capsules containing spores.
 
• They are typically** 0.2–10 cm** (0.1–3.9 in) tall, though some species are much larger.
 
• Dawsonia, the tallest moss in the world, can grow to** 50 cm **(20 in) in height. There are approximately 12,000 species.

• **Madurai Shanmukhavadivu Subbulakshmi** (16 September 1916 – 11 December 2004) was an Indian Carnatic singer from Madurai, Tamil Nadu. 
 
• She was also awarded with the Ramon Magsaysay award, Asia's highest civilian award in 1974.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Ratna** is the highest civilian award in India.
 
• The Bharat Ratna award is presented by the president of India.
 
• The first Bharat Ratna award was awarded to politician **C.** **Rajagopalachari**, philosopher Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and scientist CV Raman in the year 1954.
 
• **Indira Gandhi **was the first female Prime Minister of India and was conferred with the Bharat Ratna in 1971. She was elected as the president of the Congress party in 1959.
